config.title: Centering (all methods)

intro.title: Centering (all methods)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage that demonstrates different methods for centering elements using CSS. You will learn the core concept of aligning content both horizontally and vertically within a container. The main technologies involved are CSS properties like text-align, margin, flexbox, and grid. By the end, you will understand how to choose the right centering technique for various layout scenarios.
intro.usecase: Centering elements is fundamental to creating polished, professional interfaces across all web applications. You'll use these techniques constantly when building login forms that need to be perfectly centered on the screen, dashboard cards that align neatly in grid layouts, and modal dialogs that appear in the middle of the viewport. Whether you're working on e-commerce product displays, admin panels with data tables, or mobile-friendly navigation menus, mastering centering methods ensures your UI components look intentional and visually balanced. These skills are essential for creating responsive designs that work consistently across different screen sizes and devices.

objectives: Apply flexbox properties to horizontally and vertically center elements within a container
Configure grid layout properties to achieve precise centering of content
Implement text-align and line-height techniques for inline and text element centering
Manipulate margin and positioning properties to center block-level elements
Construct responsive centering solutions that adapt to different screen sizes
Integrate multiple centering methods within a single layout to solve complex alignment challenges
Initialize transform-based centering for elements with dynamic dimensions

steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure for centering practice
steps.instruction: Create an HTML file with a container div and three child div elements inside it. Give the container an id of 'centering-container' and give each child div a class of 'centered-item'.
steps.hint: Start with a basic HTML structure that includes a container element and three child elements that we'll center using different CSS techniques.
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <title>CSS Centering Techniques</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <!-- Add your container and child elements here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a basic HTML structure with a container and three child elements that we can apply different centering techniques to in the following steps.
successCriteria: The HTML file contains a container div with id 'centering-container' and three child div elements with class 'centered-item'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have exactly three child div elements with the correct class name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The structure isn't quite right. Remember to create a container div with id 'centering-container' and three child div elements with class 'centered-item'.

steps.title: Add CSS file and link it to HTML
steps.instruction: Create a CSS file named 'styles.css' in the same directory as your HTML file. The HTML file already has a link tag in the head section pointing to 'styles.css'.
steps.hint: You only need to create the CSS file. The HTML file is already set up to use it.
steps.analogousExample:
/* styles.css */
/* Your CSS rules will go here */
steps.seedCode:
/* styles.css */
/* Your CSS rules will go here */
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS file named 'styles.css' is created and ready for styling.
successCriteria: A CSS file named 'styles.css' exists in the same directory as the HTML file.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You created a CSS file, but make sure it's named exactly 'styles.css' and is in the same folder as your HTML file.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a CSS file named 'styles.css'. The HTML file already has a link tag pointing to it.

steps.title: Apply basic styling to container and child elements
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to style the container with a light gray background, 400px width, 300px height, and a 2px solid black border. Also style the child element with a blue background, 150px width, 100px height, and a 1px solid white border.
steps.hint: Use the .container and .child selectors. Set background-color, width, height, and border properties for each.
steps.seedCode:
/* styles.css */
/* Your CSS rules will go here */
steps.expectedOutcome: The container and child elements will have visible colors, dimensions, and borders, making them ready for centering demonstrations.
successCriteria: CSS includes .container with background-color: lightgray, width: 400px, height: 300px, border: 2px solid black, and .child with background-color: blue, width: 150px, height: 100px, border: 1px solid white.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure both .container and .child have all the required properties: background-color, width, height, and border.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS doesn't match the required styling. Check that you're using the correct selectors and property values.

steps.title: Center text horizontally using text-align
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the .container class to horizontally center all text content inside it using the text-align property.
steps.hint: Use the selector .container and set text-align to center.
steps.expectedOutcome: The text inside the .container element will be horizontally centered.
successCriteria: The .container selector has a text-align property set to center.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct property value. Check if you've set text-align to center.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to use the text-align property with the value center for the .container selector.

steps.title: Center inline elements horizontally with margin auto
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for a block-level element (like a div) to center it horizontally within its parent using margin: 0 auto.
steps.hint: Use margin: 0 auto to center a block element horizontally. This works when the element has a defined width.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule that centers a block-level element horizontally using margin: 0 auto.
successCriteria: The CSS includes a rule with margin: 0 auto for a block-level element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your CSS rule includes margin: 0 auto to center the element horizontally.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to create a CSS rule that uses margin: 0 auto to center a block-level element horizontally.

steps.title: Center vertically with line-height
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the .child class to vertically center its text using line-height equal to the container's height.
steps.hint: Set the line-height property to match the container's height (e.g., 200px) to vertically center single-line text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The text inside the .child element will be vertically centered within its container.
successCriteria: The .child rule includes line-height: 200px; to match the container's height.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but ensure line-height matches the container's height (200px).
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding a line-height property to the .child class equal to the container's height.

steps.title: Center both horizontally and vertically with Flexbox
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a class named '.flex-center' that uses display: flex, justify-content: center, and align-items: center to center content both horizontally and vertically.
steps.hint: Create a new CSS selector starting with '.flex-center' and add the three Flexbox properties inside the curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule for .flex-center that enables Flexbox centering is added to the stylesheet.
successCriteria: The .flex-center rule contains display: flex, justify-content: center, and align-items: center properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the .flex-center rule is missing one or more required Flexbox properties. Make sure to include display: flex, justify-content: center, and align-items: center.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule doesn't match the requirements. Please create a new rule for .flex-center with display: flex, justify-content: center, and align-items: center properties.

steps.title: Center with CSS Grid
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a .grid-container class that uses display: grid and place-items: center to center its content both horizontally and vertically.
steps.hint: Use the place-items property with the value 'center' to center content in both directions within a grid container.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule for .grid-container is added, enabling centering using CSS Grid.
successCriteria: The .grid-container rule includes display: grid and place-items: center.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your .grid-container rule includes both display: grid and place-items: center.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for .grid-container is missing or incorrect. It should use display: grid and place-items: center.

steps.title: Center with absolute positioning and transform
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a class named '.absolute-center' that uses position: absolute with top: 50%, left: 50% and transform: translate(-50%, -50%) to center elements.
steps.hint: Create a new CSS selector starting with '.absolute-center' and add the positioning and transform properties inside curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule for '.absolute-center' with absolute positioning and transform properties will be added to the stylesheet.
successCriteria: The '.absolute-center' rule includes position: absolute, top: 50%, left: 50%, and transform: translate(-50%, -50%).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your '.absolute-center' rule includes all four required properties: position: absolute, top: 50%, left: 50%, and transform: translate(-50%, -50%).
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for '.absolute-center' is missing or incomplete. Please add a rule with position: absolute, top: 50%, left: 50%, and transform: translate(-50%, -50%).

steps.title: Center with table-cell display
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a .table-container class that uses display: table-cell with vertical-align: middle and text-align: center to center content.
steps.hint: Create a selector for .table-container and set display to table-cell, vertical-align to middle, and text-align to center.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule for .table-container with table-cell display properties for centering.
successCriteria: The .table-container rule includes display: table-cell, vertical-align: middle, and text-align: center.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your .table-container rule includes all three properties: display: table-cell, vertical-align: middle, and text-align: center.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for .table-container is missing or incorrect. Please add a .table-container selector with the required table-cell display properties.

steps.title: Create comparison examples of all methods
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a .comparison-container class that will hold multiple examples of centering methods side by side.
steps.hint: Define a CSS class that uses display: flex to arrange child elements horizontally.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS class .comparison-container is created with flexbox properties to arrange multiple examples horizontally.
successCriteria: The .comparison-container class is defined with display: flex and appropriate spacing properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include display: flex and some spacing properties like gap or margin.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for .comparison-container is missing or doesn't use flexbox for horizontal arrangement.

steps.title: Add responsive considerations for centering
steps.instruction: Add a media query that changes the container's centering method to flexbox on screens smaller than 768px.
steps.hint: Use @media (max-width: 768px) to target smaller screens, then apply display: flex and justify-content: center to the .container class.
steps.expectedOutcome: The centering technique will adapt to different screen sizes, using flexbox for mobile devices.
successCriteria: A media query targeting max-width: 768px is added and applies flexbox centering to the .container class.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your media query targets screens smaller than 768px and applies display: flex and justify-content: center to .container.
steps.feedbackWrong: The media query is missing or incorrect. Remember to use @media (max-width: 768px) and apply flexbox centering to .container.
